reviewQueue.title: Independent review of rotation PR
reviewQueue.label: Analysis, not truth
reviewQueue.analysisNote: Prepared analysis of fix/staging-cred-rotation. Findings are claims with evidence — not an approval.

findings.title: Retry behavior may conflict with RFC §4.2
findings.body: Implementation sets MAX_RETRIES = 5. RFC §4.2 requires staging rotations fail closed after three retries. Test rotateCreds.retries.spec.ts asserts five attempts. Two callers inherit the constant.

evidence.title: RFC · Credential lifecycle · §4.2
evidence.excerpt: Staging rotations MUST NOT exceed three retries before failing closed.

findings.title: Deploy lock held for full retry window
findings.body: Rotation acquires the staging deploy lock for the entire retry window (~90s at five attempts). Callers in deploy-pipeline and nightingale-cron both wait on the same lock.

findings.title: No rollback path if third-party secret store lags
findings.body: If Vault accepts the write but the staging runtime still serves the old secret, the PR has no documented rollback. RFC §5 mentions a dual-publish window; this change does not implement it.

evidence.title: RFC · §5 Dual-publish window
evidence.excerpt: New and old credentials MUST both validate for at least one deploy cycle.

reviewQueue.scopeFooter: Examined 8 files · 2 callers · 1 RFC · 14 tests. Absence of findings is not approval.

rfc-cred.title: RFC: Credential lifecycle
rfc-cred.body:
## §4.2 Retry budget

Staging rotations MUST NOT exceed three retries before failing closed. Each retry may wait at most 18 seconds. The deploy lock MUST NOT be held longer than the maximum retry window (3 × 18s = 54s).

Rationale: longer lock windows starve nightingale and partner staging deploys. Production may use a higher budget under incident commander approval.

## §5 Dual-publish window

New and old credentials MUST both validate for at least one deploy cycle before the old secret is revoked. Implementations that skip dual-publish require an explicit RFC exception filed in #infra.
